result.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not; it reproduces at three independent levels, and the numerical core is stronger than the reporter's own evidence.

MECHANISM (confirmed). /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/steer.py:283-290 applies the C7 rule (guidance/B01.yaml:97, `action: dedup_key, pattern: "@price", to: Close`) as `re.sub(r"\b(Close|Open|High|Low|Vwap)\b", "Close", s)` over the whole canonical STRING, per occurrence. So the key keeps no record of which price positions shared a field. Verified: `dedup_key('sub(High, Low)') == dedup_key('sub(Close, Open)') == dedup_key('sub(High, Close)') == 'sub(Close,Close)'`, and `div(sub(Close,Low),sub(High,Low))` and `div(sub(High,Close),sub(High,Low))` both give `div(sub(Close,Close),sub(Close,Close))`. Exhaustively: of the 25 ordered price pairs, ALL 25 land in one key for `sub`, `div` and `day_corr`, and 20/25 for `day_cov`.

FIRES IN THE REAL SEARCH (confirmed). I installed the exact idea_search dedup clause (scripts/idea_search.py:219-224) over trees from the real `alphacube.mining.generator.TypedTreeGenerator` (CPU, no data needed; its fields are `CUBE_FIELDS = (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, Vwap, Ret, Amt)`, i.e. the names the regex matches). Over 3000-6000 proposals, 6-7% of all `equivalent` rejections are over-collapses — the dropped tree is not reachable from the retained one by renaming ONE price field (the only operation C7's evidence measured). Worst observed form: the retained representative is a degenerate same-leaf expression and the informative sibling is dropped unscored, e.g. kept `day_corr(Vwap, Vwap)` / dropped `day_corr(High, Low)`; kept `day_signed_ratio(Open, Open)` / dropped `day_signed_ratio(High, Vwap)`; kept `day_wstd(Close, Close)` / dropped `day_wstd(Open, Vwap)`. On synthetic data: `day_corr(High, High)` is identically 1.0 (cross-sectional std 0.0) while `day_corr(High, Low)` has real dispersion (std 6.2e-2); `sub(High, High)` is identically 0 while `sub(High, Low)` is the daily range. The constant panel fails the `dist >= 0.5` gate AND permanently owns the key, because `first_form` is cleared only in `install(arm)`.

LIVE ON THE CORPUS (confirmed, independently). Grouping all 2839 scored sweep_s3 variants (7041 across s1-s3) by `dedup_key`: 10 buckets hold more than one distinct canonical form; 4 of them are over-collapses under the single-field-rename test. The reporter's 1.07 figure is real but their cited example is the weak one. The actual smoking gun is F109_erm_mag_gap_5m_tsm20, where one key holds 9 distinct forms with utrain long_sharpe from -0.57 to -1.64, and the sweep records each member's own measured correlation to the base: `leaf_Close_low` (one of 20 Close leaves swapped, corr_orig 0.928, uls -1.04) is merged with `fld_Close_Low` (all 20 swapped, corr_orig 0.490, uls -0.57) and `fld_Close_Vwap` (corr_orig 0.447, uls -0.66) and `v_base` (uls -1.24). Correlations of 0.45-0.49 are nowhere near the "rho 0.96~0.98" C7's `why` claims, so the merge is not supported even on the data the rule was derived from. F112_scale_spow_masktop likewise merges 9 forms with a 1.03 spread (the reporter's `v_base` 0.74 / `leaf_High_close` 0.79 pair is a corr-0.971 single-leaf swap and does not demonstrate the bug; the bucket's real over-collapse is `leaf_High_*` mixed with `leaf_Close_*`). F110 and F115 are the other two.

CONCRETE LOSS INSIDE A DEFINED IDEA. Idea I4_intraday_reversal_tail's own seed is `cross_ema(pow_3(sub(div(day_last(Close), day_first(Open)), 1)), 30)` - two different price leaves. All 25 spellings of `div(day_last(@price), day_first(@price))` inside that structure share one key, so I4's steer arm scores exactly one of {open-to-close return, close-to-open, high-to-low range ratio, ...}.

TWO INACCURACIES IN THE REPORT (neither saves it). (1) "one experiment whose representative is identically 0" - the dedup key string is never evaluated; the scored object is `first_form[key]`, the first raw spelling proposed. The substance survives because the retained representative can itself be a degenerate same-leaf expression, which I reproduced. (2) The rejection does not waste evaluation budget: `TypedTreeGenerator.generate` retries up to `max_retries*4` = 64 times and `mutate_subtree` / `mutate_operator` return None on refusal. The cost is permanently lost coverage for the arm, not burned GPU time - the fix should not be scoped as a budget fix.

Latent second site: steer.py:315, `accept(expr, u=None)` salts its hash with `dedup_key`, so all 25 price-pair spellings of one `sub`/`div` tree would receive the same accept/reject draw when thinning a fixed list. No current caller uses `u=None` (idea_search passes `u=self._rng.random()`), so this is not live today.

result.corrected_fix:
The finding is real; the suggested fix is partly wrong and incomplete. Three defects in it:

1. "refuse to collapse when the substitution would make any sub/div have two identical operands" is an operator whitelist and leaks. I reproduced the identical collapse under day_corr, day_cov, day_wstd, day_wmean, day_topw_mean and day_signed_ratio. Patching sub/div fixes none of the cases I actually observed in the generator.
2. "Only apply the leaf collapse when the canonical form contains at most one distinct price leaf" still merges `v_base` (all Close) with `fld_Close_Low` (all Low) and `fld_Close_Vwap` (all Vwap) - each has exactly one distinct price leaf, and in F109 those measure corr_orig 1.000 / 0.490 / 0.447 with uls -1.24 / -0.57 / -0.66.
3. "rename the FIRST distinct price leaf to Close, the second to Close2" is the right shape but also insufficient for the same reason as (2).

Correct fix, in order of what each step buys:

(a) steer.py:283-290 - stop doing a regex substitution over the string. Walk the canonical TREE and relabel price leaves by first appearance: the k-th distinct price field encountered becomes `@P<k>`, then rebuild the key from the tree. This makes the key invariant exactly under a bijection of price fields, which is the most the rule could ever claim. It separates `leaf_Close_low` (P1...P2...P1) from `fld_Close_Low` (P1 everywhere), and `day_corr(High, High)` (P1,P1) from `day_corr(High, Low)` (P1,P2), with no operator list to maintain. Note the current code also only fires on rules whose `pattern.tree.name in LEAF_KINDS`, so the same tree walk should handle @flow the same way.

(b) (a) is necessary but not sufficient: it still merges a tree with its whole-field renames, and F109 shows that merge measuring corr_orig 0.447-0.490 against the base. So C7 should not be a hard dedup at all. Change guidance/B01.yaml:97 from `action: dedup_key` to `action: weight` with w < 1 (0.2-0.3 matches the other D-rules), and leave `dedup_key` to the exact-equivalence rewrites C1-C6. `Guidance.accept(e, u=self._rng.random())` already thins per draw, so a sibling that loses one draw can still be proposed and scored later - which is the behaviour the evidence supports, instead of a permanent exclusion. Keep the honest claim in `why`: the 0.96-0.98 figure holds for single-occurrence leaf swaps on some factors, not for field-wide substitution (F109 fld_Close_Vwap 0.447, F115 leaf_Close_vwap 0.761, F108 leaf_Close_low 0.763).

(c) scripts/idea_search.py:221-224 - `first_form` is a one-way gate for the whole arm (cleared only in `install`), so even with a correct key the first spelling wins forever. If the hard gate is kept, make it prefer a non-degenerate incumbent: when the stored representative contains a binary node whose two operands are the same leaf (value identically 0 / 1 / constant), replace it with the new candidate instead of rejecting. Also count over-collapses separately from `stats['equivalent']` so the episode record shows how much coverage the gate cost.

(d) tests/test_steer.py:97 currently asserts only the licensed case (`ts_spearman(day_quantile(Low),10)` == `ts_spearman(day_quantile(Close),10)`). Add the negative assertions: `dedup_key('sub(High, Low)') != dedup_key('sub(Close, Open)')`, `dedup_key('day_corr(High, High)') != dedup_key('day_corr(High, Low)')`, and `dedup_key('div(sub(Close, Low), sub(High, Low))') != dedup_key('div(sub(High, Close), sub(High, Low))')`.

(e) Separately (latent, not live): steer.py:315 salts the no-`u` accept hash with `dedup_key`, so under the current key all 25 price-pair spellings of one tree share a single accept/reject draw. Fix (a) resolves this too; no current caller passes `u=None`.
